_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with KRAS-mutated recurrent low-grade serous ovarian cancer (LGSOC) who have received prior systemic therapy; approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and duration of response.

pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with measurable KRAS-mutated recurrent LGSOC who had received at least one prior systemic therapy, including a platinum-based regimen.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) assessed by blinded independent review committee (BIRC) per RECIST v1.1, with duration of response (DoR) as an additional outcome.
pivotal_trials.result: Confirmed ORR 44% (95% CI 31, 58), with complete response 3.5% and partial response 40%; duration of response ranged 3.3 to 31.1 months.

key_safety: Most common (≥25%) adverse reactions were increased creatine phosphokinase, nausea, fatigue, increased AST, rash, diarrhea, musculoskeletal pain, and edema. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 32% of patients (most common: sepsis 9%); fatal adverse reactions occurred in 3.6%. Notable warnings include ocular toxicities.
target_moa: Avutometinib is a MEK1 inhibitor that induces inactive RAF/MEK complexes and prevents MEK1/2 phosphorylation by RAF in the RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK (MAPK) pathway; defactinib is an inhibitor of FAK and proline-rich tyrosine kinase-2 (Pyk2).
companion_dx_detail: No FDA-approved companion diagnostic is available; KRAS mutation status was determined by local NGS or PCR testing, and a companion diagnostic is in development (a PMC in the accelerated approval).

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred for discussion at an Oncology Drug Advisory Committee meeting.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Tumor response rate (ORR) and duration of response.

citations.quote: This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and duration of response [see *Clinical Studies* (14)]. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Complete the ongoing confirmatory trial RAMP 301 (NCT06072781), a Phase 3 randomized open-label study of avutometinib plus defactinib versus investigator's choice, providing progression-free survival and final overall survival analyses to verify clinical benefit.

citations.quote: Complete the ongoing trial titled, “RAMP 301: A Phase 3, Randomized, Open-Label Study of Combination Therapy with Avutometinib plus Defactinib Versus Investigator’s Choice of Treatment in Patients with Recurrent Low-Grade Serous Ovarian Cancer (LGSOC)”, and provide the progression-free survival and the final overall survival analyses, intended to describe and verify the clinical benefit of avutometinib and defactinib in combination in adult patients with recurrent, KRAS-mutated low grade serous ovarian cancer. Include central KRAS testing results for all patients.
To verify clinical benefit, the Applicant should complete the ongoing confirmatory trial, RAMP-301 (NCT06072781).

basis.text: Breakthrough therapy designation was granted on 20 May 2021 for avutometinib in combination with defactinib for patients with LGSOC with recurrent disease after 1 or more prior lines of therapy including platinum-based chemotherapy.

requirement.text: 4835-4 Conduct a clinical trial to characterize and evaluate the potential serious risk of cardiomyopathy related to the use of the combination of avutometinib and defactinib in adult patients with recurrent, low grade serous ovarian cancer.

citations.quote: 4835-4 Conduct a clinical trial to characterize and evaluate the potential serious risk of cardiomyopathy related to the use of the combination of avutometinib and defactinib in adult patients with recurrent, low grade serous ovarian cancer. The trial should include serial monitoring of blood pressure, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), high-sensitivity troponin, and N-terminal brain natriuretic peptide. The cardiac assessments must include a sufficient number of patients, over a sufficient time period, to systematically determine the incidence of LVEF reductions \ge 10\% from baseline. A randomized trial design is preferred given the unknown population risk. Include an analysis of the risk, and monitoring and mitigation measures.
